title: Keto Peanut Butter Cup Cupcakes
shortDescription: Keto peanut butter cupcakes with a chocolate buttercream swirl, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These keto peanut butter cupcakes taste like your favorite candy in cake form. I tested this batter three times in my own kitchen to get the crumb soft, not dry, which is the biggest problem with almond flour cakes. The peanut butter batter uses natural peanut butter and almond flour, so it stays low carb without turning gritty. A swirl of chocolate buttercream on top gives you that classic peanut butter cup pairing in every bite. I balance the texture by adding sour cream to the batter. It keeps the cupcakes moist for two days on the counter, which matters a lot with keto baking. Top each one with a sugar free chocolate peanut butter cup for a fun finish and extra crunch.
ingredients: 1/3 cup natural peanut butter, no sugar added
2/3 cup granulated erythritol or monk fruit blend
12 sugar free chocolate peanut butter cups, for garnish
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350°F and line a muffin pan with 12 paper liners.
In a bowl, whisk almond flour, baking powder, and salt together. Set aside.
Beat 1/2 cup butter, peanut butter, and erythritol together until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each. Stir in vanilla and sour cream.
Fold in the dry mix until just combined. Do not overmix or the batter turns dense.
Divide batter evenly between liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 10 minutes, then move to a rack.
For the buttercream, beat 1 cup butter until pale, then add cocoa powder and powdered erythritol.
Add heavy cream and beat on high for 3 minutes until light and smooth.
Pipe the chocolate buttercream in a tall swirl on cooled cupcakes and top each with a peanut butter cup.
tips: Use natural peanut butter with no added sugar. Regular sweetened peanut butter changes the carb count.
Let cupcakes cool completely before piping, or the buttercream will slide off.
If your buttercream looks grainy, add cream one teaspoon at a time until it smooths out.
Store cupcakes in the fridge up to 5 days, but let them sit 15 minutes at room temperature before eating.

faq.question: Can I use peanut butter powder instead of regular peanut butter?
faq.answer: Yes, but add a bit more butter to the batter. Peanut butter powder soaks up more liquid and can dry out the crumb without that extra fat.

faq.question: Why did my keto cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means the pan opened too early or the batter was overmixed. Check doneness at 16 minutes and avoid stirring the batter past the just combined stage.

faq.question: Are sugar free peanut butter cups actually keto friendly?
faq.answer: Most brands made with allulose or erythritol work well for keto. Check the label for net carbs per cup, since brands vary a lot.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes nut free?
faq.answer: Not easily. Both almond flour and peanut butter are the main flavor and structure here, so swapping both changes the recipe significantly.

recipeKeys: low carb chocolate peanut butter dessert
conclusion: These keto peanut butter cup cupcakes hit that sweet and salty spot without the sugar crash. The soft peanut butter crumb and rich chocolate swirl make them feel like a real treat. Bake a batch and see how fast they disappear from the counter.
